questions.stem: What risk does a Data Glossary help to mitigate?
questions.explanation: A Data Glossary is described as a vital step towards mitigating the risk of creating a potential Data Swamp.

questions.stem: Under which umbrella discipline do the Data Glossary and Data Dictionary fall?
questions.explanation: Data Glossary versus Data Dictionary falls under the umbrella of Metadata Management.

questions.stem: What does a Data Glossary contain?
options: Business terms that provide meaning and context
questions.explanation: A Data Glossary includes business terms such as region, sales, quantity, brand and year that give meaning and context to data.

questions.stem: How is a Data Dictionary described in contrast to a Data Glossary?
options: As a collection of business terms in non-technical language
As a list of dashboards owned by each department
As a set of data science models
As a repository housing names, definitions and attributes of data elements
As a backup catalogue of database objects
questions.explanation: A Data Dictionary houses the names, definitions and attributes of data elements, whereas a Glossary is a searchable collection of business terms.

questions.stem: Which of the following can a comprehensive Data Glossary refer to?
options: Tables, schemas, databases, reports, dashboards and data science models
questions.explanation: A comprehensive Data Glossary can refer to tables, schemas and databases; reports and dashboards; and data mining and data science models.

questions.stem: What proportion of redundant objects can consulting a Data Glossary reduce?
questions.explanation: Checking the glossary before creating a new object prevents reinvention and can reduce up to 80% of redundant objects.

questions.stem: How does a Data Glossary reduce redundancy?
options: By letting users check whether an equivalent object already exists before creating a new one
By merging all dashboards into one
questions.explanation: Before creating a new object, users consult the glossary to see whether an equivalent dashboard, report, table, schema or model already exists.

questions.stem: Who normally interacts with a Data Glossary?
questions.explanation: The Data Glossary is aimed at business users without deep technical expertise; 'Normally, business folks interact with Data Glossary.'

questions.stem: In the example glossary terms region, sales, quantity, brand and year, what would an analyst quickly conclude about the table?
options: That it holds employee payroll data
That it holds server log data
That it relates to sales data with quantities by brand at a regional level
That it is a security audit table
questions.explanation: Those terms tell anyone analysing the table that it relates to sales data, with quantities likely provided brand-wise at a regional level.

questions.stem: What does combining a Data Glossary with a Data Dictionary achieve?
options: It replaces the need for a database
It converts the glossary into a security policy
It makes the glossary an integral part of metadata management
questions.explanation: When combined with a Data Dictionary, the Data Glossary becomes an integral part of metadata management.
